title: Preserve provider-native quota errors in existing worker and readiness observation

owned: Antigravity adapter and auth-probe invocation-log binding (--log-file) so provider-native error text is observable
supervisor.detect_worker_failure native-log fallback for AGY error_message-only streams
reassignment fallback message preserving a qualified source's prior task["next"] instructions
not_changing: reconcile_unavailable_assignments candidate selection and process/lease fencing
composes_with: the active Git authentication delivery task (shares antigravity.py's spawn_background_process call but owns .orchestrator/test_adapter_delivery_policy.py; that file is intentionally not touched here)

failure_reproduction.case: `agy --output-format stream-json` retries a RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED/429 quota error internally and only emits opaque step_update/error_message records on stdout with no error text; `agy --prompt` auth/quota probes can also authenticate and then hit quota with a clean exit and empty stdout/stderr.
failure_reproduction.prior_outcome: supervisor.detect_worker_failure returned None for the error_message-only stream (no authoritative envelope ever reached stdout), and provider_permissions._antigravity_probe_ready classified the empty-output probe as a silent not-logged-in auth failure instead of quota_reached, even though the same invocation had already authenticated.
failure_reproduction.regression: test_antigravity_error_observability.py's test_error_message_only_stream_falls_back_to_native_log_quota and test_empty_output_probe_reclassifies_as_quota_from_native_log reproduce both gaps against fake local CLI log fixtures with no network or credentials.

implementation.native_log_binding: adapters/antigravity.py and provider_permissions.py's _antigravity_auth_probe both add an explicit --log-file <path> to the exact CLI invocation, using the CLI's own existing --log-file flag; the adapter reports the bound path via DeliveryResult.metadata["native_log_path"], which supervisor.py stores on the worker record.
implementation.detect_worker_failure_fallback: supervisor.native_log_failure() scans the bound native log newest-line-first for a small set of provider-native quota/auth markers only after the existing stdout-stream scan finds nothing, so a later actual quota failure supersedes an earlier superseded not-logged-in startup notice and existing authoritative-envelope detection is unchanged.
implementation.probe_reclassification: provider_permissions._probe_once merges the bound native log's text into the same `combined` string _antigravity_probe_ready already inspects (signature unchanged), so existing quota-before-auth precedence in _antigravity_probe_ready applies unmodified; the probe deletes its own transient native log after each read.
implementation.reassignment_next_preservation: reconcile_unavailable_assignments' ordinary (non-load-balance) fallback branch now appends its short recovery reason to any existing qualified task["next"] instead of the no-receipt persistence path silently overwriting them, while not nesting onto an already-generic prior recovery note.
implementation.no_new_authority: No new classifier, cooldown store, recovery command, or provider identity grouping is introduced; classify_worker_failure's existing quota_terminal markers and model_rotation's existing cool_slot/fallback logic consume the recovered text unchanged.

passed.result: 20 passed, 2 subtests passed (unchanged; confirms Git-authentication-owned adapter tests are unaffected)

review_decision.note: Independently verify the invocation-log binding on both the adapter and probe paths, the newest-line-first native-log fallback precedence, the reassignment next-preservation regressions, and that .orchestrator/test_adapter_delivery_policy.py was left untouched.
